A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EventPAR dataset and OTN-RWKV framework. All supplied pages, including equations, tables and figures, are readable. Both documents end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments on EventPAR and two public datasets, together with input, fusion, aggregation, threshold and backbone ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises numerous measurements, and adds an emotion-specific comparison in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The visual encoders, similarity-based event-token filtering, asymmetric OTN-RWKV fusion, prediction head and weighted cross-entropy objective remain unchanged. Condensed explanations and the notation correction in Equation 2 do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EventPAR and the simulated-event versions of MARS-Attribute and DukeMTMC-VID-Attribute. EventPAR retains 100K samples and 50 attributes, including six emotions. The new emotion comparison examines existing labels rather than adding task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes HAP, reducing the EventPAR benchmark from 18 comparators to 17. Table 4 retains its six comparators. The new emotion comparison uses Label2Label, VTB, PromptPAR and RethinkingPAR, all already included in the main benchmark.

E3.justification: The reported threshold sweep shrinks from seven settings to five, dropping 0.70 and 0.85 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 8). v2 also adds evaluation restricted to the existing emotion attributes. The stated public-dataset splits, metrics, preprocessing and Section 5.2 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds an analysis of emotion recognition against four baselines. Conversely, v2 removes the separate stepwise-fusion comparison and two threshold points. The input, aggregation and backbone analyses remain; the retained portions of v1 Table 8 are reorganized into v2 Tables 7 and 9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new emotion chart also reports point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 3 extensively revises baseline scores and resource measurements. VTB mA changes from 76.96 to 88.41, now exceeding OTN-RWKV's revised 87.70. In Table 4, OTN-RWKV F1 changes from 82.18 to 83.22 on MARS and 79.38 to 82.78 on Duke, while comparator scores remain unchanged. Ablation values also change, and Figure 7 adds emotion results. These are reported-result revisions; their experimental basis is not explained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and metric definitions are retained, with no added proofs or theoretical results. Equation 2 corrects 'whv' to the already defined 'wkv'; this is a notation correction rather than revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the benchmark contribution from retraining 18 methods to 17. The central claims about the first RGB-Event PAR dataset, emotion attributes, asymmetric RWKV fusion and state-of-the-art performance remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation that the emotion results demonstrate effective emotional-cue capture. Its Duke discussion removes the earlier qualification about trailing VTB and emphasizes adaptability. It also adds a specific comparison limitation: 2025 methods were not evaluated because their code was unavailable.

D1.justification: v2 removes Table 3's baseline-code links and the disclosure that approximately 20 students participated in collection and annotation. Splitting the combined ablation table also removes explicit aggregation/fusion control columns. The training and hardware details, and the promised project code/data release link, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References to HAP, DeepFool and the adversarial-attacks review are removed. The related-work sections and the paper's positioning relative to PAR, event vision and RWKV otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial passages throughout Sections 3–5 are rewritten and compressed. The separate data-collection subsection disappears, with some content retained elsewhere; the method overview, benchmark discussion, ablation explanations and prediction-visualization discussion are extensively shortened, and the ablation narrative is reordered.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially expanded with additional examples and temporal emotion illustrations, and a new emotion-results chart becomes Figure 7. Table 3 loses its code column and changes highlighting; the combined ablation table is split into separate displays. Several displays move, while the original token-selection figure becomes Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful emotion-specific evidence and clearer dataset illustrations, but removes baseline-code links, annotation-participation details and some fusion-ablation evidence. Extensive benchmark-score replacements are unexplained, and Section 5.3 still quotes older EventPAR values despite Table 3's revisions. These mixed effects and the uncertain basis of the revised results prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
